notes: Independent Round-2 verifier answers. Only reviews/blind/E.json consulted. No question/*, no content-card, no round1 files, no resolutions read at this stage.

answers.rationale: HLO dot with lhs_contracting_dims={1}, rhs_contracting_dims={0} is a standard matmul contracting A[m,k] and B[k,n]; d = A@B has shape [128,64]; ROOT r = add(d,C) is elementwise bias addition. A/C/D are basic mischaracterizations.
IREE is an MLIR-based AOT compiler lowering StableHLO / linalg / tosa to a serialized VM module (.vmfb) plus device-specific artifacts; runtime dispatches via HAL supporting multiple backends.
Compiler is heavy AOT; runtime is small/embeddable so edge/mobile devices need not host the MLIR toolchain.

Fragment 1's bounds/indices are affine in IVs+symbols (%N, %M). Fragment 2's inner-loop upper bound %kidx comes from a runtime memref.load, so it is data-dependent (not a symbol under affine semantics) — verifier rejects.
applyFullConversion requires every remaining op to be legal per ConversionTarget; unmatched illegal ops → verification failure. A/B/D each misstate MLIR framework behaviour.

Trait = static compile-time metadata; Interface = virtual dispatch; Dialect = grouping namespace enabling progressive lowering. C is false: ops can be aliased/lowered across dialects via interfaces and conversion patterns.

4 blocks × 256 threads/block = 1024; memspace 1 = global under gpu-to-nvvm convention documented in options; real bug is %idx = %bid + %tid — should be %bid * blockDim.x + %tid so indices don't collide across blocks.
iterator_types [parallel, parallel, reduction] with maps (m,k)/(k,n)/(m,n) and body mulf then addf into out = standard matmul with accumulation into %C.
strided<[8,1], offset:0> with shape 4x8 → row-major (last stride 1); [i,j] at i*8+j elements from base; memspace 3 = GPU workgroup/shared per gpu-dialect convention.
Operation contains 0+ Regions; each Region has Blocks in CFG; SSA Values flow at runtime; Attributes are compile-time metadata. A/C/D each invert or fabricate rules.
MLIR PassManager runs op-scoped passes over matching ops; nested pass managers (e.g., func.func nested inside ModuleOp) compose hierarchical pipelines. B/C/D are false.
arith canonicalizers fold add-zero → %x, mul-one → %x, sub %x,%x → 0; unused constants are DCE'd during canonicalize which iterates to a fixed point.

B and C describe tensor (value/SSA) vs memref (buffer, aliasable, memspace/strides). A is wrong — bufferization is essential. D is wrong — the standard lowering pipeline is tensor → bufferize → memref → scf → vector → LLVM; vector is not the primary lowering target for arith ops on tensor prior to bufferization, and tensors are commonly bufferized then vectorized.
ONNX is an interchange format; runtimes make perf choices; two runtimes on same ONNX model can differ in perf though numerics agree within tolerance. C, D confuse format with runtime.
Models declare opset_import version(s); each op's semantics is defined by that version — consumers must implement it.
ONNX supports named symbolic dynamic dims; onnx.shape_inference propagates static/symbolic info; unresolved dims stay symbolic.
IR version defines ModelProto schema/structure; opset version defines operator semantics; both are independent and must be declared in a model.
StableHLO is a versioned operator set with formal spec serving as portability contract between frameworks and compilers with fwd/bwd compatibility guarantees.
Decouples release cycles of frameworks and compilers, avoiding the O(F × C) integration matrix and enabling shared optimization work.
BYOC / extern-op lowers a Relax op to an opaque call into a library; the compiler treats it as a black box for fusion/scheduling but still tracks shape/dtype at the graph level.

Graph-level fusion in Relax + loop-level fusion in TensorIR (compute_inline / reverse_compute_at) are both real. C over-generalizes; D is false — external calls remain opaque and cannot be inlined as loop bodies.
MetaSchedule: rule-based space expansion over TensorIR + cost model + real measurement, iterative.
Relax adds first-class symbolic/dynamic shapes, cross-level (graph <-> PrimFunc), Python-native metaprogramming — capabilities Relay's typed functional core could not cleanly express.

B canonical bind-only; C canonical split+bind vector-add; D cache_read shared. A false — vectorize is not guaranteed to succeed and does not silently emit scalar; it raises a schedule/verifier error when preconditions fail.
PrimFunc is loop-level tensor program with explicit blocks/iters/buffers; schedule primitives transform loop structure but preserve compute semantics.
Relax VM = bytecode runtime dispatching PrimFunc/external calls/control flow, handling dynamic-shape allocation and object lifetime while graph structure is statically compiled.
Buffer assignment is a static compile-time pass that maps HLO SSA values to physical buffers, letting disjoint-liveness values share buffers and enabling in-place when input is provably last-used.

XLA has multiple fusion kinds (loop/input/output) chosen by memory-access patterns; elementwise + reduction can be output-fused. C is false — fusion has cost-based boundaries. D is false — kFusion is a compiler-side HloInstruction.

A: StableHLO has dynamic_* ops. C: serving mitigates recompilation via bucketing/padding. D: XLA is static-first, shape changes trigger recompilation. B is wrong — HLO retains shape annotations, which optimizations depend on.
GSPMD takes sharding-annotated HLO and rewrites it into a per-device program, inserting collectives (all-reduce/all-gather/reshard) where required to preserve semantics.
